item.title: SPC Oct 18, 2026 1300 UTC Day 1 Convective Outlook
item.description:
SPC 1300Z Day 1 Outlook 
Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0730 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

Valid 181300Z - 191200Z

...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms are not forecast through tonight.

...Synopsis and Discussion...
Even with east-northeasterly low-level flow persisting to the north
of a remnant cold front, diurnal heating of a moist airmass will
support sufficient instability for isolated to scattered
thunderstorms across parts of south FL and the Keys today.
Occasional lightning flashes may also occur with convection across
parts of the Southwest ahead of a low-amplitude mid-level shortwave
trough. Weak shear across south FL and limited moisture/instability
over AZ/NM will hinder the potential for severe thunderstorms across
both regions. Dry and/or stable conditions will preclude
thunderstorms for the remainder of the CONUS through the period.

..Gleason/Kerr.. 10/18/2026

item.title: SPC Oct 18, 2026 1630 UTC Day 1 Convective Outlook
item.description:
SPC 1630Z Day 1 Outlook 
Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1114 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

Valid 181630Z - 191200Z

...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms are not forecast through tonight.

...Synopsis...
Tranquil conditions will exist across much of the contiguous United
States through tonight.  Extensive surface high pressure influencing
much of the central and eastern U.S. will favor offshore flow into
the northern Gulf of America and feature a seasonably dry/stable
airmass.  A few weak thunderstorms are possible over south FL and
the Keys to the north of a surface front undergoing frontolysis
across the southern Gulf and FL Straits.  Farther west, an upper
trough migrating northeast across the Four Corners will be
associated with isolated showers/thunderstorms across parts of the
Southwest.

..Smith/Supinie.. 10/18/2026

item.title: SPC Oct 18, 2026 1730 UTC Day 2 Convective Outlook
item.description:
SPC 1730Z Day 2 Outlook 
Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1158 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

Valid 191200Z - 201200Z

...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms are not expected on Monday.

...Synopsis...
An upper low will linger off the East Coast while an upper trough
amplifies just off the West Coast. Meanwhile, a leading wave will
affect the area from Baja CA into the Four Corners states.

Instability will be minimal over most of the CONUS due to an area of
high pressure, with the surface ridge extending from the Great
Lakes/Upper Midwest to the Gulf Coast. The exceptions will be near
the FL Keys where moist easterly winds will persist, supporting
scattered showers and a few thunderstorms, and over AZ and NM, where
midlevel moisture will support weak instability. In either case,
severe weather is not anticipated due to weak instability.

..Jewell.. 10/18/2026

item.title: SPC Day 1 Fire Weather Outlook
item.description:
SPC Day 1 Fire Weather Outlook 
Day 1 Fire Weather Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1139 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

Valid 181700Z - 191200Z

...NO CRITICAL AREAS...

The ongoing fire weather forecast remains on track with no
highlighted areas across the CONUS; please see the previous
discussion for additional information.

..Elizalde-Garcia.. 10/18/2026

.PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 0106 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026/

...Synopsis...
A closed mid/upper low will remain positioned off of the East Coast
today, with upper-level ridging stretching from the southern Plains
into the Ohio Valley. Weak upper troughing will persist across
southern California and portions of the Southwest, and a robust
mid-level shortwave trough will begin to approach the Pacific
Northwest coastline towards the end of the period. At the surface,
high pressure will be maintained across the Mid-Atlantic, with a
second area of surface high pressure building into the northern
Plains behind a progressive cold front. Recent widespread
precipitation across much of the Intermountain West, Plains, and
East will largely temper fire weather concerns across these regions
today.

Some guidance suggests that sustained southwesterly winds may
increase to around 15 mph amid minimum RH values in the 15-25% range
across portions of northeastern CA, southern/southeastern OR, and
northwestern NV, where ERCs are noted to be around the 80-90th
percentiles. Confidence in a sustained period of overlap of elevated
wind/RH criteria remains too low to warrant elevated highlights, but
brief periods of locally elevated fire weather conditions may
materialize should areas of stronger winds overlap RH below 20%.

Dry and breezy conditions are also forecast today across portions of
the southern/central High Plains preceding a lee surface trough and
separately across portions of the Southeast, including parts of GA,
SC, and AL, along the southern periphery of surface high pressure to
the north. Poor to marginal fuels, recent rainfall across parts of
these areas, and borderline wind/RH conditions (10-15 mph winds
across the Southeast and 20-25% minimum daytime RH across the
Plains) are expected to temper the overall fire weather threat
across these regions, however.

...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov/fire for graphic product...
